findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.comment:
Observed food items such as but not limited to lettuce heads and other vegetables stored on the floor of the walk in cooler. Discussed with PIC and vegetables were placed on shelves. Ensure that food items are stored at least 6 inches from the floor or in a manner that protects against contamination. 

3-305.11: (A) FOOD shall be protected from contamination: In clean dry location, not exposed to any form of contamination, at least 6 inches above floor. (B) FOOD in working containers and packages may be stored less than 6 inches on case lot handling EQUIPMENT. (C) Pressurized BEVERAGE containers, cased FOOD in waterproof containers, and milk containers in plastic crates may be stored on floor.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.12: During the inspection, an employee was observed to wash their hands and shut off the faucet without using a barrier. This heavier was corrected on site and the employee rewashed their hands with correct procedure. PIC will retrain staff on hand washing. Ensure staff wash their hands following correct hand washing procedures. 
2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-601.11: 
-The gaskets of the refrigerators and freezers in the kitchen are observed to have an accumulation of dust/food debris. Ensure the current accumulation of dust/food debris is cleaned and sanitized to remove the current accumulation and then ensure these surfaces are cleaned and sanitized at a frequency necessary to maintain them clean. 
-The white shelving above the triple sink is observed to have an accumulation of dust and is in need of being cleaned. Ensure that the shelving is cleaned of the current accumulation and then is cleaned at a frequency necessary to maintain it clean. 
4-601.11: (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-101.11: The wall panel directly above the triple sink is observed to have an apparent gap present where the panel has lifted away from the wall. Ensure this panel is repaired or replaced to create a smooth, nonabsorbent, and easily cleanable surface. 
6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent. (B) In TEMPORARY FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, floor may be material effectively treated to control dust and mud. Walls and ceilings may be material that protects interior from weather and windblown dust and debris.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.16: The mop is observed to be stored with the mop head directly on the floor and unable to air dry. This mop was inverted and placed in a position able to air dry during the inspection. Ensure the mop is stored in a manner that allows it to air dry between uses.
6-501.16: After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to airdry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:

Ensure these surfaces are cleaned to remove the current buildup of accumulation and then ensure these surfaces are cleaned at a frequency necessary to maintain them clean. 
6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
3-302.11: The top of the white freezer next to the microwave is observed to have an excessive accumulation of dust/soil debris. On this surface is stored single service to-go containers. The bottom container is being discarded during today’s inspection and the sing service items are being moved from this location and will not be stored on this surface until it is cleaned and sanitized. 
3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment:
4-101.11: The shelf in the back corner of the kitchen that holds the bowls is currently covered with contact paper that is heavily damaged and soiled. The bowls are not in contact with the paper on the food contact surface and so the facility has been advised to remove the contact paper and either change it out with new paper that is changed at a frequency necessary to maintain it clean or to remove the contact paper and replace it with a plastic or metal sheeting that is smooth, nonabsorbent, and easily cleanable.
4-101.11: (A) Materials used for FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES may not allow migration of deleterious substances shall be safe. P Materials used for FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES may not allow migration of deleterious substances shall be: (B) Durable, nonabsorbent, and CORROSION-RESISTANT (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness (D) SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, scratching, decomposition, and distortion. C

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:

(P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
3-501.16: The walk-in cooler was recorded at 58 degrees F at the start of the inspection. The cooler was observed in operating order during the hours of prep before the facility opened today which was less than 4 hours ago. The food items requiring cold holding below 41 degrees F and the eggs which require under 45 degrees F were moved into the white fridge along the cook line that was holding temperature. No food items remain in the cooler that are potentially hazardous at this time. Observation of the cooler will be made towards the end of the inspection to observe the temperature again. If records show the cooler above 41 degrees F, main entrance is required on the cooler. Facility has stated they will monitor the temperature again in the morning and call for service at that time if necessary.
3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less.

Ensure the practice is established and continues for the hand sink purpose.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.citation_text:
5-205.11  (Pf) Hand washing sink blocked by sponge and steel wool. Hand washing sinks must be accessible at all times. Reference 5-205.11.

Observed a sponge and steel wool to be inside hand sink at facility prior to inspector washing hands. Maintain all hand sinks free of items in order to be accessible at all times. COS.

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used
findings.citation_text:
3-501.13  (C) Frozen fish is thawing while still wrapped in reduced oxygen packaging (ROP). Packaging must be removed from fish in ROP prior to thawing under refrigeration or running water. Reference 3-501.13.

Observed frozen fish to be thawing while still wrapped in reduced oxygen packaging (ROP) within walk-in cooler. Discussed thawing fish outside of ROP in order to hinder foodborne illness.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.citation_text:
4-901.11  (C) Equipment/Utensils are not properly Air-Dried after cleaning and sanitizing at front drink area. After cleaning and sanitizing all equipment and utensils shall be air dried before use. Reference 4-901.11.

Observed multiple plastic cups to have condensation within and stacked properly at front drink area. Allow cups to adequately air-dry after cleaning and sanitizing before stacking. Discussed with PIC.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.citation_text:
4-602.13  (C) Soil residue present on multiple freezers throughout facility and walk-in cooler fan. Clean all non-food contact surfaces frequently to prevent soil accumulation.  Reference 4-602.13.

Observed multiple facility freezers to have food and/or soil debris within. Observed walk-in cooler fan to have a large accumulation of dust. Discussed routine cleaning of non-food contact surfaces with PIC.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.citation_text:
6-201.11  (C) Hand sinks were found in a state of disrepair, or not to be smooth and easily cleanable. Except as specified in Section 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are smooth and easily cleanable.  Reference 6-201.11.

Observed multiple hand sinks to be in need of caulk and/or re-caulking (both customer bathrooms and hand sink within kitchen). Discussed repairs with PIC.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment:
Front door has small gap in the bottom corner and along the side of the door that may allow for pest entry, and there are mouse droppings observed in several areas of the facility (bottom shelves in the kitchen with a significant amount, one on the rice container near the back door, and a few on a top shelf in the dry storage). PIC states that Orkin was just here this morning, but they no longer leave an invoice at the time of service. PIC states Orkin gives them glue traps to put down, but there is only one glue trap observed set up. Seal door to prevent pest entry and consult Orkin to eliminate pests. 

6-202.15  (C) Exterior door allows access for pests. Exterior doors shall be: 1) self-closing, 2) solid and tight fitting, 3) limited to designed use. Reference 6-202.15.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.111  (Pf) The premises shall be maintained free of insects, rodents and other pests. Eliminate pests, using proper pest control processes as needed. Reference 6-501.111.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment: Facility has the Purrell Food Contact Surface spray bottles that they use on prep surfaces, but do not have the appropriate test strips for this product. Contact the company on the label to purchase test strips for this product.
findings.citation_text: 4-302.14  (Pf) Test kits or other devices are not available to the employees to measure sanitizing solution concentration. Provide a test kit or other measuring device so the employees can measure concentrations and ensure proper sanitization. Avoid a concentration of sanitizer that is too high, which can be toxic. Reference 4-302.14.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment: There are mouse droppings observed on the bottom shelves in the kitchen, one on the rice container near the back door and a few on the top shelf in the dry storage area. Clean these shelves.
findings.citation_text: 4-602.13  (C) Clean all non-food contact surfaces frequently to prevent soil accumulation.  Reference 4-602.13.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment: Dish machine sanitizer dispenser unit is not operating. Machine does have a hot water booster, but the disc thermometer run through the machine two times only reached a maximum of 156F. Facility thought that something was wrong with the electrical portion of it and had it worked on, but the dispenser needs parts that will have to be ordered. In the meantime, PIC states that they are sanitizing in the 3 compartment sink. This sink will need to be set up to sanitize all dishware after being run through the dish machine for the wash and rinse portion of the wash, rinse, sanitize process. A spot check will be conducted once dish machine has been repaired to ensure that it is operating properly. 4-501.114  (P) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution. Options: 25ppm to 49ppm when the temperature is at least 120°F and the pH is 10 or less; or (2) 50ppm to 99ppm when the temperature is at least 100°F and the pH is 10 or less, or when the temperature is at least 75°F and the pH is 8 or less; or (3) 100ppm when the temperature is at least 55°F and the pH is 10 or less. Reference 4-501.114.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.comment: Observed a hat and other personal items stored on a food prep surface. Do not store personal items where they have the potential to contaminate food and food prep areas. Store personal items in designated areas away from food and food prep areas. 6-305.11  (C) Employee clothing and personal items were found stored improperly. Food establishments shall A) Provide designated dressing rooms or dressing areas for employees that routinely change their clothes in the establishment; B) Provide lockers or other suitable facilities for the orderly storage of employees' clothing and other possessions. Reference 6-305.11.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment: Facility has 4 food handler certificates available and 2 of them are for 2 of their Certified Food Protection Managers. All food handlers who do not have the Certified Food Protection Manager Certificate will need to complete the online ANSI approved food handler training course and have a certificate available. Make sure to check expiration dates for those certificates that are available as several expire in August of this year. 410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement.  Reference 410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430.

findings.title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory
findings.comment:
Squirt bottles of food were unlabeled as to their contents.  Label the bottles or the place where they are set to identify each bottle's contents.

750-130f Unless its identity is unmistakable, bulk food such as cooking oil, syrup, salt, sugar or flour not stored in the product container or package in which it was obtained, shall be stored in a container identifying the food by common name.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment:
Opened ready-to-eat potentially hazardous food (pineapple) in a refrigerator was undated as to when the can was opened.  The food was moved to a commercial container and the container dated to CORRECT the violation.  The can had not been opened more than 7 days.

750-151(a) Refrigerated potentially hazardous food held at the establishment more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked with the ate or day by which the food shall be consumed, sold, or discarded. Maximum holding time at 41°F is 7 days. Properly date mark food and do not hold longer than 7 days.

findings.title: Potentially hazardous foods properly thawed
findings.comment:
Four containers of pork were thawing at room temperature.  They were put in the walk-in cooler to continue thawing in the proper manner to CORRECT the violation.

750-240 Potentially hazardous foods shall be properly thawed by one of the  following method. 1. Under refrigeration 41°F or below, 2. Under  potable running water 70°F or below or below with sufficient water velocity to agitate and float off loose food particles into the over-flow, 3. In microwave as part of the cooking process, 4. As part of the cooking process.

findings.title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
findings.comment:
An opened can of pineapple and an opened can of pineapple were uncovered in refrigeration units.  The food in each can was moved to food grade containers and covered to CORRECT the violation.    (NOTE: Once opened, do not store acidic food like ketchup in the can.  Move it to a food grade container.)

750-120(a) Food shall be protected at all times. Properly store and protect food.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment:
1.  The under side of the shelf to the right of the door to the customer area was unpainted.  Paint the underside of the shelf.
2.  The boards around the top of the walk-in cooler (inside it) were unpainted.  (REPEAT VIOLATION)   
Paint all unsealed boards with a light colored glossy paint so they are non-absorbent and easily cleanable.

750-690 Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices and readily accessible for cleaning, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:

750-800(b) To prevent cross contamination, kitchenware and food contact surfaces of equipment shall be washed, rinsed, and sanitized after each use.

750-860 Cleaned and sanitized utensils an equipment shall be stored at least six inches above the floor in a clean, dry location in a way that protects them from contamination by splash, dust and other means.

findings.title: Restrooms with self-closing doors, fixtures operate properly, facility clean, supplied with hand soa...

750-1120 All restrooms must have self-closing doors, properly operating fixtures, be clean and have proper hand washing supplies in order to help facilitate good hygienic practices.  Provide properly designed and maintained restrooms.

750-1170 Openings to the outside shall be protected against the entrance of rodents and insects.

1. Potentially hazardous food in the walk-in cooler was 47-51 degrees.  The food was discarded to correct the violation.
2. Potentially hazardous food in the refrigerator by the can opener was 44-45 degrees.  The food was moved to a colder refrigerator to correct the violation.
3. Potentially hazardous food in the walk-in cooler was also not dated as to when it was placed in the walk-in cooler.  The food was discarded.

750-120(a) Potentially hazardous foods, shall be maintained at a proper product temperature at all times during storage (41°F or below, or 135°F or above)
750-151(a) Refrigerated potentially hazardous food held at the establishment more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked with the ate or day by which the food shall be consumed, sold, or discarded. Maximum holding time at 41°F is 7 days. Properly date mark food and do not hold longer than 7 days.

findings.title: Facilities to maintain proper temperatures
findings.comment:
1.  The walk-in cooler was 47-51 degrees.   Repair the cooler.
2.  The refrigerator by the can opener was 45 degrees.  The thermostat was turned down to correct the violation.

750-140 All refrigeration units used to store potentially hazardous foods shall be able to maintain proper product temperature at 41°F or below.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment:
The boards around the walk-in cooler (window and the shelf above the window on the kitchen side were unsealed wood.  Paint or cover the wood with a smooth, non-abosrbent material.

750-690 Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices and readily accessible for cleaning, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
The following non-food contact surfaces were soiled:
  1.  bottom inside of the two freezers near the back exterior door.
  2.  outside surfaces of the garbage disposal under the spray hose  (REPEAT VIOLATION) 
  3.  surfaces inside the fryer door (REPEAT VIOLATION)  
  4.  pipes and under side of shelf above the cooking equipment  (REPEAT VIOLATION)
  5.  surfaces on both wok stands to the left and right of stove  (REPEAT VIOLATION)
  6.  both sides of stove next to woks  (REPEAT VIOLATION)
  7.  side of wood cabinet next to right hand wok  (REPEAT VIOLATION)
Clean these surfaces.

750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Storage/handling of clean equipment, utensils
findings.comment:
Saucers and bowls were stored food side up on the shelf to the right of the door to the waitress station.  They were inverted to correct the violation.

750-860 Cleaned and sanitized utensils an equipment shall be stored at least six inches above the floor in a clean, dry location in a way that protects them from contamination by splash, dust and other means.

findings.title: Plumbing installed and maintained
findings.comment:
There is a leak in the refrigeration unit inside the walk-in cooler.  Repair the leak.

750-1060 All plumbing shall be sized, installed, and maintained in accordance with applicable provisions of the Illinois State Plumbing Code. Repair fixtures in accordance with the Illinois Plumbing Code.

findings.title: Containers covered, adequate number, insect and rodent proof, emptied at proper intervals, clean
findings.comment:
A dumpster lid was open.  (REPEAT VIOLATION).   Keep the dumpster lids closed.

750-1130a Garbage and refuse shall be kept in durable easily cleanable, insect-proof, and rodent-proof containers.

findings.title: Outer openings protected from insects, rodent proof
findings.comment:
The back exterior door would not close all the way on its own and there were gaps around it.  Repair the door so it is self-closing and tight fitting
.
750-1170 Openings to the outside shall be protected against the entrance of rodents and insects.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment:
1.  The threshold of the back exterior door was soiled. (REPEAT VIOLATION)    Clean the threshold.
2.  Coving is missing on the wall-to-floor junctions in the walk-in cooler.  (REPEAT VIOLATION)   Place coving on the wall.

750-1220 Floors shall be kept clean.
750-1200 The junctures between walls and floors shall be coved and sealed, or shall not present an opening of more that 1/32 of an inch.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment:
1.  The walk-in cooler is in the process of being re-done.  Cover all the unprotected wall surfaces and seal all gaps.
2.  There is a gap between the counter top that the microwave sets on and the wall.   Seal the gap.

750-1210 All walls and ceilings must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Provide properly constructed and clean walls and ceilings.
750-1210(b) Walls and ceilings in walk-in refrigeration units, food preparation areas, equipment washing areas, and toilet rooms shall be smooth, light-cored, non-absorbent, and easily cleanable.

findings.title: Lighting provided as required.  Fixtures shielded
findings.comment:
1.  A light cover is broken above the can opener.  (REPEAT VIOLATION)    Replace the cover or put protective plastic tubes on each individual fluorescent bulb.
2.  Light bulbs are uncovered in a ceiling fixture in the back room with exterior door.    Replace the cover or put protective plastic tubes on each individual fluorescent bulb.

750-1240 All lights in the food prep, food storage or kitchen area of a establishment must be properly shielded (i.e. either have a physical shield or be a shatter resistant bulb) so as to reduce the potential for cross contamination in case of breakage.  Provide properly shielded lights.

findings.title: Premises maintained fee of litter, unnecessary articles. Cleaning and maintaining equipment properly...
findings.comment:
There are weeds growing around the outside of the building, especially inside the wood fence.   Cut the weeds.

750-1350The entire premises shall be maintained free of litter, rubbish, unnecessary articles, weeds, and travel of unnecessary persons.
